syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Diversity in the living world and biodiversity

concepts.learning_objective: Explain biodiversity as the number and types of organisms on earth, each kind representing a species.
Distinguish the technical question of what living is from the philosophical question of the purpose of life.
Explain why standard scientific names are needed and how naming depends on correct identification under ICBN and ICZN.
Apply the universal rules for writing a binomial scientific name, including the author's abbreviation.
Describe classification as grouping into convenient categories called taxa that exist at different levels.
State the basic processes of taxonomy and explain the scope of systematics.

topics.title: Taxonomic categories: species, genus and family

concepts.learning_objective: Identify species and genus as categories, using specific epithets and genera from common examples.
Explain family as a group of related genera characterised by vegetative and reproductive features.

topics.title: Order, class, phylum, kingdom and the taxonomic hierarchy

concepts.learning_objective: Place organisms in order, class, phylum or division and kingdom using examples from the chapter and Table 1.1.
Interpret how shared characteristics change as one moves up the taxonomic hierarchy.

topics.title: Changing systems and the five kingdom classification

concepts.learning_objective: Trace how classification moved from Aristotle's and Linnaeus' systems to Whittaker's five kingdoms and why the two kingdom system was inadequate.
State Whittaker's criteria and compare the five kingdoms on cell type, wall, body organisation and nutrition.
Identify bacterial shapes and distinguish photosynthetic, chemosynthetic and heterotrophic bacteria.
Explain how archaebacteria survive extreme habitats and name halophiles, thermoacidophiles and methanogens.
Describe eubacteria, cyanobacteria with heterocysts, mycoplasma and bacterial reproduction.
Describe the walls and ecological roles of diatoms and dinoflagellates, including diatomaceous earth and red tides.
Explain the pellicle and mixed nutrition of euglenoids and the plasmodium and spores of slime moulds.
Distinguish the four groups of protozoans with examples.
Describe hyphae, mycelium, chitin walls and saprophytic, parasitic and symbiotic fungi.
Sequence plasmogamy, karyogamy, dikaryophase and meiosis in the fungal sexual cycle.
Compare phycomycetes, ascomycetes, basidiomycetes and deuteromycetes by mycelium, spores and examples.
State the features of Kingdom Plantae, including partially heterotrophic plants and alternation of generations.
State the features of Kingdom Animalia: wall-less cells, holozoic nutrition and food reserves.
Describe the discovery, structure and genetic material of viruses and the diseases they cause.
Distinguish viroids and prions from viruses.
Explain lichens as a symbiosis of phycobiont and mycobiont and their use as pollution indicators.

topics.title: Systems of classification in the plant kingdom

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish artificial systems such as that of Linnaeus from natural systems such as that of Bentham and Hooker.
Explain that phylogenetic systems are based on evolutionary relationships and assume a common ancestor for members of a taxon.
Identify numerical taxonomy, cytotaxonomy and chemotaxonomy as aids to classification.
Describe algae as chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic, largely aquatic organisms of varied form.
Distinguish vegetative, asexual and sexual reproduction in algae, including isogamy, anisogamy and oogamy.
State the ecological and commercial uses of algae such as agar, algin, carrageen and Chlorella.

topics.title: Classes of algae: Chlorophyceae, Phaeophyceae and Rhodophyceae

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the pigments, stored food, cell wall and flagella of green algae.
Describe the pigments, stored food, body organisation and reproduction of brown algae.
Describe the pigments, stored food, habitat and reproduction of red algae.
Explain why bryophytes are called amphibians of the plant kingdom and state their ecological importance.
Explain the dominant haploid gametophyte and the dependent diploid sporophyte of bryophytes.
Compare the plant body and reproduction of liverworts and mosses, including gemmae and protonema.
Describe the dominant vascular sporophyte and the free-living prothallus of pteridophytes.
Explain heterospory and why it is regarded as a precursor to the seed habit.
Classify pteridophytes into Psilopsida, Lycopsida, Sphenopsida and Pteropsida with examples.
Describe the roots, stems and leaves of gymnosperms and their adaptations.
Explain heterospory, strobili, the reduced gametophytes and the formation of naked seeds in gymnosperms.
State the defining features, range of size and classes of angiosperms.
Distinguish gymnosperms from angiosperms on the basis of ovules and seeds.
Identify cellular, tissue, organ and organ-system levels of organisation with examples.
Distinguish complete from incomplete digestive systems and open from closed circulatory systems.
Distinguish asymmetrical, radially symmetrical and bilaterally symmetrical body plans.

topics.title: Germ layers, coelom, segmentation and notochord

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish diploblastic from triploblastic animals on the basis of embryonic layers.
Classify animals as coelomates, pseudocoelomates or acoelomates from the nature of the body cavity.
Explain metameric segmentation and the notochord as bases of classification.
Describe the water canal system, skeleton and reproduction of sponges.
Explain cnidoblasts, polyp and medusa forms and metagenesis in cnidarians.
Identify the distinctive features of ctenophores such as comb plates and bioluminescence.
Describe the features and parasitic adaptations of flatworms.
Describe the pseudocoelomate body plan and features of roundworms.
Describe metamerism, circulation, excretion and reproduction in annelids.
Describe the features and economically important examples of arthropods.
Describe the body plan of molluscs including mantle, shell and radula.
Describe the water vascular system of echinoderms and the body plan of hemichordates.
State the fundamental characters that distinguish chordates from non-chordates.
Compare urochordates, cephalochordates and vertebrates on the basis of the notochord.
Compare cyclostomes, cartilaginous fishes and bony fishes.

topics.title: Tetrapoda: Amphibia, Reptilia, Aves and Mammalia

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the distinguishing features of amphibians and reptiles.
Describe the features of birds, including those that help in flight.
Identify the unique features of mammals and classify examples.
Distinguish tap, fibrous and adventitious root systems with their origin and examples.
Identify the regions of a root tip and the function of each.

topics.title: The stem and the structure of a leaf

concepts.learning_objective: State the origin, features and functions of the stem that distinguish it from the root.
Describe the leaf base, petiole and lamina and the role of each.

topics.title: Venation, types of leaves and phyllotaxy

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish reticulate and parallel venation and relate them to dicots and monocots.
Distinguish simple, pinnately compound and palmately compound leaves.
Identify alternate, opposite and whorled phyllotaxy with examples.

topics.title: Inflorescence and the general features of a flower

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish racemose and cymose inflorescences by growth of the axis and order of flowers.
Classify flowers by symmetry and by the number of floral appendages.
Classify flowers as hypogynous, perigynous or epigynous from the position of the ovary.
Identify valvate, twisted, imbricate and vexillary aestivation with examples.
Describe the stamen and the cohesion and adhesion of stamens.
Describe the carpel, apocarpous and syncarpous ovaries and the types of placentation.
Describe the pericarp of a fruit, drupes and parthenocarpic fruits.
Describe the structure of a dicotyledonous seed and endospermic and non-endospermous seeds.
Describe the structure of a monocotyledonous seed such as maize.

topics.title: Semi-technical description and the family Solanaceae

concepts.learning_objective: Read and interpret the symbols of a floral formula and a floral diagram.
Recognise the vegetative and floral characters and economic importance of Solanaceae.
Describe the structure of the epidermis and the role of the cuticle in preventing water loss.
Describe the structure of stomata, guard cells and subsidiary cells that form the stomatal apparatus.
Distinguish unicellular root hairs from the usually multicellular trichomes of the shoot and state their roles.
Identify the tissues and regions that make up the ground tissue system, including mesophyll in leaves.
Classify vascular bundles as radial or conjoint and as open or closed on the basis of xylem-phloem arrangement and cambium.
Describe the tissue layers of a dicot root from the epiblema to the stele, including endodermis and pericycle.
Compare monocot and dicot roots in the number of xylem bundles, size of pith and secondary growth.
Describe the hypodermis, cortex, endodermis, pericycle, vascular bundles and pith of a young dicot stem.
Identify the features of a monocot stem and use them to tell it apart from a dicot stem.
Describe the epidermis, palisade and spongy mesophyll and vascular system of a dorsiventral (dicot) leaf.
State how an isobilateral (monocot) leaf differs from a dorsiventral leaf in stomata, mesophyll and vascular bundles.
Explain how bulliform cells in grass leaves help reduce water loss under water stress.
Define a tissue and recall that complex animals have only four basic tissue types.
Explain how tissues form organs and organs form organ systems, showing division of labour.
Distinguish morphology (external form) from anatomy (internal organs) in animals.
Identify the class, phylum and common Indian species of frog.
Explain why frogs are called cold-blooded or poikilotherms.
Describe camouflage, aestivation and hibernation as adaptations of frogs.
Describe the moist, mucus-covered skin of the frog and its role in water uptake.
Identify the external features of the frog's head, trunk and limbs.
Distinguish male and female frogs by vocal sacs and copulatory pads.

topics.title: Digestive and respiratory systems of frog

concepts.learning_objective: Trace the parts of the frog's alimentary canal and relate its length to diet.
Explain the roles of HCl, gastric juice, bile and pancreatic juice in digestion.
Compare cutaneous and pulmonary respiration in the frog.

topics.title: Circulatory and excretory systems of frog

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the frog's three-chambered heart, closed circulation and portal systems.
Distinguish blood from lymph and recall that frog RBCs are nucleated.
Describe the frog's excretory organs and explain why it is ureotelic.
Classify parts of the frog's nervous system into central, peripheral and autonomic divisions.
Identify the parts of the fore-brain, mid-brain and hind-brain of the frog.
Identify the frog's sense organs and distinguish well-organised ones from cellular aggregations.

topics.title: Reproduction in frog and its importance

concepts.learning_objective: Trace the path of sperms through the male reproductive system of the frog.
Describe the female reproductive system, external fertilisation and tadpole development.
Explain the ecological and economic importance of frogs.

topics.title: What is a Cell? and Cell Theory

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the cell is regarded as the fundamental structural and functional unit of life.
Describe the contributions of Leeuwenhoek, Brown, Schleiden, Schwann and Virchow to cell theory.
Distinguish prokaryotic from eukaryotic cells on the basis of a membrane-bound nucleus and organelles.
Identify membrane-bound and non-membrane-bound organelles and where ribosomes occur in a cell.
Compare the sizes and shapes of different cells and relate shape to function.
State the general features of prokaryotic cells, including the nucleoid, plasmids and mycoplasma.
Describe the bacterial cell envelope, mesosomes, flagella, pili and fimbriae.
Describe 70S prokaryotic ribosomes, polysomes and inclusion bodies.
Explain the composition of the plasma membrane and the fluid mosaic model.
Distinguish simple diffusion, osmosis, carrier-mediated passive transport and active transport.
Describe the composition of the cell wall, primary and secondary walls, middle lamella and plasmodesmata.
Identify the organelles that make up the endomembrane system and those that do not.
Describe the structure and functions of the rough and smooth ER and the Golgi apparatus.
Describe the structure and functions of lysosomes and vacuoles, including the tonoplast.
Describe the double-membrane structure of mitochondria and relate it to aerobic respiration.
Classify plastids into chloroplasts, chromoplasts and leucoplasts and state their roles.
Compare 70S and 80S ribosomes and explain the meaning of the Svedberg unit.
State the components and functions of the cytoskeleton.
Describe the 9+2 axoneme of eukaryotic cilia and flagella.
Describe the cartwheel structure of centrioles and their role in basal bodies and spindle formation.
Describe the nuclear envelope, nuclear pores and the nucleolus.
Describe the composition of chromatin and the DNA content of human chromosomes.
Classify chromosomes by the position of the centromere.
Describe how grinding tissue in trichloroacetic acid separates an acid-soluble pool from an acid-insoluble fraction.
Compare the elemental composition of living tissue and earth's crust and explain what wet weight, dry weight and ash reveal.

topics.title: Small biomolecules: amino acids, lipids and nucleotides

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the substituent groups of an alpha-amino acid and classify amino acids by their R groups.
Distinguish fatty acids, glycerides and phospholipids and relate saturation and melting point to fats and oils.
Distinguish nitrogen bases, nucleosides and nucleotides with examples.
Distinguish primary from secondary metabolites and give examples of secondary metabolites.
Explain the molecular-weight basis of micromolecules and macromolecules and why lipids appear in the acid-insoluble fraction.
Explain why proteins are heteropolymers and relate examples of proteins to their functions.
Compare cellulose, starch, glycogen, inulin and chitin in composition, structure and role.

topics.title: Nucleic acids and structure of proteins

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the components of a nucleotide and distinguish DNA from RNA by their sugar and bases.
Describe the primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary levels of protein structure.

topics.title: Enzymes: chemical reactions and how enzymes act

concepts.learning_objective: State the nature of enzymes and ribozymes and the role of the active site.
Interpret reaction rates, enzyme-catalysed acceleration and the idea of a metabolic pathway.
Explain how enzymes lower activation energy through formation of the enzyme-substrate complex.
Explain the effect of temperature and pH on enzyme activity, including optimum values and denaturation.
Interpret how reaction velocity changes with substrate concentration up to Vmax.
Explain competitive inhibition using the example of malonate and succinic dehydrogenase.
Classify enzymes into the six classes based on the reactions they catalyse.
Distinguish apoenzyme, prosthetic groups, co-enzymes and metal ion cofactors with examples.
Describe the cell cycle as interphase and M phase and state their relative durations.
Explain the events of G1, S and G2 phases and the change in DNA content and chromosome number.
Explain the quiescent stage (G0) and identify cells that enter it.
Identify the key events of prophase and metaphase of mitosis.
Identify the key events of anaphase and telophase of mitosis.
Distinguish cytokinesis in animal cells from that in plant cells.
Explain how a multinucleate syncytium arises when karyokinesis is not followed by cytokinesis.
State the roles of mitosis in growth, repair and continuous plant growth.
Explain why cell growth makes division necessary to restore the nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio.
Identify organisms and stages in which haploid cells divide by mitosis.
State the key features of meiosis as a reduction division.
Describe the events of leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene and diakinesis.
Describe metaphase I, anaphase I and telophase I and their outcome.

topics.title: Meiosis II and significance of meiosis

concepts.learning_objective: Describe interkinesis and the stages of meiosis II.
Distinguish the events of mitosis from those of meiosis.
Explain how meiosis conserves chromosome number and increases genetic variability.

topics.title: What we know and early experiments

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the classic experiments of Priestley, Ingenhousz, Sachs and Engelmann and what each revealed about photosynthesis.
Explain van Niel's inference that the oxygen released by green plants comes from water and use the balanced equation of photosynthesis.
Relate the membrane system and the stroma of the chloroplast to the reactions that occur in each.
Distinguish light reactions from the carbon (dark) reactions and explain why the term dark reaction is a misnomer.
Identify the four leaf pigments separated by paper chromatography by their colours.
Interpret the absorption spectrum of chlorophyll a against the action spectrum of photosynthesis.
Explain the roles of accessory pigments and why chlorophyll a is the chief pigment.
Describe the light harvesting complexes and the reaction centres P700 and P680 of PS I and PS II.
Trace the path of electrons from PS II to NADP+ in the Z scheme.
Explain how splitting of water associated with PS II replaces electrons and releases oxygen and protons.
Compare cyclic and non-cyclic photophosphorylation in terms of photosystems involved and products formed.
Explain how a proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane drives ATP synthesis through ATP synthase.

topics.title: Use of ATP and NADPH: the Calvin cycle

concepts.learning_objective: Identify RuBP as the CO2 acceptor and 3-PGA as the first stable product of the C3 pathway.
Describe carboxylation, reduction and regeneration as the three stages of the Calvin cycle.
Calculate the ATP and NADPH used by the Calvin cycle for CO2 fixed and glucose formed.
Describe the Kranz anatomy of C4 leaves and the features of bundle sheath cells.
Trace the steps of the Hatch and Slack pathway between mesophyll and bundle sheath cells.
Explain photorespiration in C3 plants and why it is absent in C4 plants.
State Blackman's law of limiting factors and apply it to a given situation.
Analyse how light intensity and CO2 concentration affect the rate of photosynthesis in C3 and C4 plants.
Explain how temperature and water stress influence the rate of photosynthesis.

topics.title: Do plants breathe? Cellular respiration and gas exchange

concepts.learning_objective: Define cellular respiration and respiratory substrates and explain why energy is released stepwise and stored as ATP.
Explain how plants meet their gas-exchange needs through stomata, lenticels and air spaces without respiratory organs.
Describe the site, discoverers and sequence of reactions of the EMP pathway.
Identify the steps of glycolysis that use or form ATP and NADH + H+ and calculate its energy yield.
Describe how pyruvic acid is converted to ethanol or lactic acid and the enzymes involved.
Explain the low energy yield and hazards of fermentation and their consequences.

topics.title: Aerobic respiration: link reaction, TCA cycle and ETS

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate to acetyl CoA in the mitochondrial matrix.
Trace the reactions of the Krebs' cycle and the points where CO2, NADH, FADH2 and GTP are formed.
Explain the electron transport system, the role of oxygen and ATP synthesis by ATP synthase.
Calculate the theoretical net ATP gain per glucose and evaluate the assumptions behind it.
Compare fermentation and aerobic respiration in breakdown of glucose, ATP yield and NADH oxidation.
Identify the points at which fats and proteins enter the respiratory pathway.
Explain why the respiratory pathway is considered amphibolic rather than catabolic.
Define respiratory quotient and state its values for carbohydrates, fats and proteins.
Calculate RQ from a balanced equation or gas-exchange data and interpret the substrate used.

topics.title: Growth: definition, open growth and measurement

concepts.learning_objective: Define growth as an irreversible permanent increase in size accompanied by metabolism.
Explain how meristems give plants an open, indeterminate form of growth with primary and secondary growth.
Identify the parameters used to measure growth in different plant parts.

topics.title: Phases of growth and growth rates

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the meristematic, elongation and maturation phases of growth.
Distinguish arithmetic and geometric growth and use their equations and curves.
Compare absolute and relative growth rates of growing systems.
Explain the roles of water, oxygen and nutrients in plant growth.
Explain how temperature and environmental signals such as light and gravity affect growth.
Describe differentiation and the structural changes cells undergo while maturing.
Distinguish dedifferentiation and redifferentiation with examples.
Explain why differentiation in plants is open and depends on the position of a cell.
Describe development as the sum of growth and differentiation and its sequence in a plant cell.
Explain plasticity using examples of heterophylly.
Classify the intrinsic and extrinsic factors that control plant development.

topics.title: Plant growth regulators: characteristics and discovery

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the chemical nature of the major plant growth regulators.
Classify plant growth regulators as growth promoters or growth inhibitors.
Recall how each major group of plant growth regulators was discovered.
Describe the physiological effects and applications of auxins.
Describe the physiological effects and applications of gibberellins.
Describe the physiological effects and applications of cytokinins.

topics.title: Ethylene, abscisic acid and interaction of PGRs

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the physiological effects and agricultural uses of ethylene.
Explain why abscisic acid is called the stress hormone and list its effects.
Evaluate how PGRs act synergistically or antagonistically in plant events.
Identify animals that exchange gases by diffusion over the body surface, a moist cuticle or tracheal tubes.
Distinguish branchial, pulmonary and cutaneous respiration with examples from invertebrates and vertebrates.
Trace the path of air from the external nostrils to the alveoli and describe the lungs and pleura.
Distinguish the conducting part from the respiratory or exchange part and state their functions.
Explain why the air-tight thoracic chamber is essential for breathing and list the steps of respiration.
Explain inspiration and expiration in terms of intra-pulmonary and atmospheric pressure.
Describe the roles of the diaphragm, intercostal and abdominal muscles in changing thoracic volume.
Define TV, IRV, ERV and RV and use their average values in calculations.
Derive IC, EC, FRC, VC and TLC by adding the appropriate respiratory volumes.
Interpret the partial pressures of O2 and CO2 at different sites to predict the direction of diffusion.
Explain how solubility and the thin three-layered diffusion membrane favour gas exchange at the alveoli.
Describe how O2 is carried by haemoglobin and plasma and how much O2 blood delivers to tissues.
Interpret the sigmoid oxygen dissociation curve and the factors that favour binding or release of O2.
Explain the transport of CO2 as bicarbonate, carbamino-haemoglobin and dissolved CO2, with the role of carbonic anhydrase.

topics.title: Regulation of respiration and respiratory disorders

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the roles of the respiratory rhythm centre in the medulla and the pneumotaxic centre in the pons.
Explain how the chemosensitive area and receptors of the aortic arch and carotid artery respond to CO2 and H+.
Identify asthma, emphysema and occupational respiratory disorders from their causes and effects.
Describe the composition of plasma and the roles of its major proteins, and distinguish plasma from serum.
Describe the types, numbers and functions of erythrocytes, leucocytes and platelets.
Relate the antigens and antibodies of the ABO groups to donor compatibility in transfusion.
Explain Rh grouping and how Rh incompatibility causes erythroblastosis foetalis and can be prevented.
Describe the sequence of reactions by which fibrinogen is converted to a fibrin clot.
Explain the roles of platelets, tissue factors and calcium ions in initiating and supporting clotting.
Explain how interstitial fluid forms from blood and how it differs from plasma.
State the functions of lymph and the lymphatic system, including fat absorption through lacteals.

topics.title: Circulatory pathways and the human heart

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish open and closed circulatory systems with examples.
Compare the hearts and circulation of fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals.
Describe the chambers, septa, valves and nodal tissue of the human heart.
Describe the sequence of systole, diastole, valve movements and heart sounds in a cardiac cycle.
Calculate cardiac output and cardiac cycle duration from stroke volume and heart rate.
Interpret the P-wave, QRS complex and T-wave of a standard ECG and use it to find heart rate.

topics.title: Double circulation and regulation of cardiac activity

concepts.learning_objective: Trace the pulmonary and systemic circulations and the hepatic portal and coronary systems.
Explain why the heart is myogenic and how neural and hormonal signals moderate cardiac output.
Interpret blood pressure readings and identify hypertension and its effects.
Explain the cause of coronary artery disease and the symptom of angina.
Distinguish heart failure from cardiac arrest and heart attack.

topics.title: Nitrogenous wastes and excretory structures in animals

concepts.learning_objective: Classify animals as ammonotelic, ureotelic or uricotelic and relate each mode to the toxicity of the waste and water availability.
Identify protonephridia, nephridia, Malpighian tubules, green glands and kidneys with the animal groups that have them.
Describe the position and internal structure of the human kidney, including hilum, pelvis, calyces, cortex, medulla and columns of Bertini.
Describe the parts of a nephron and the order in which filtrate passes through them.
Distinguish cortical and juxtamedullary nephrons by the length of the loop of Henle and the vasa recta.
Explain ultrafiltration across the three layers of the glomerular filter and the role of podocytes.
State the normal GFR and use filtrate and urine volumes to show that about 99 per cent of the filtrate is reabsorbed.
Explain how tubular secretion of H+, K+ and ammonia maintains ionic and acid-base balance.
Describe reabsorption and selective secretion in the proximal convoluted tubule.
Explain how the permeability of the two limbs of Henle's loop concentrates and then dilutes the filtrate.
Describe the roles of the distal convoluted tubule and collecting duct in water, ion and pH balance.

topics.title: Mechanism of concentration of the filtrate

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the counter current mechanism operating between Henle's loop and the vasa recta.
Describe the medullary osmotic gradient, the solutes that cause it and its role in concentrating urine.
Explain how osmoreceptors, the hypothalamus and ADH regulate water reabsorption.
Trace the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone sequence and its effect on blood pressure and GFR.
Explain how atrial natriuretic factor acts as a check on the renin-angiotensin mechanism.

topics.title: Micturition and role of other organs in excretion

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the micturition reflex from bladder stretch to the release of urine.
State the normal characteristics of human urine and interpret abnormal constituents such as glucose and ketone bodies.
Describe the excretory roles of the lungs, liver, sweat glands and sebaceous glands.
Explain uremia and the working of haemodialysis using an artificial kidney.
Evaluate kidney transplantation as the ultimate correction of kidney failure and why a related donor is preferred.
Identify renal calculi and glomerulonephritis from their descriptions.

topics.title: Movement, locomotion and types of cellular movement

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish movement from locomotion and give the purposes of locomotion.
Identify amoeboid, ciliary and muscular movements shown by human cells.
State the origin and the special properties of muscle tissue.
Compare skeletal, visceral and cardiac muscles by location, appearance and control.

topics.title: Structure of skeletal muscle and contractile proteins

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the organisation of a skeletal muscle into fascicles, fibres and myofibrils.
Identify the A band, I band, Z line, M line and H zone of a sarcomere.
Describe the structure of actin and myosin filaments and their regulatory proteins.
Explain the sequence of events from a neural signal to cross bridge formation.
Explain contraction as sliding of thin filaments and its effect on the bands.
Distinguish red and white muscle fibres and explain muscle fatigue.
State the composition and the axial and appendicular divisions of the human skeleton.
Describe the vertebral column, sternum and the types of ribs.
Identify the bones of the limbs and the pectoral and pelvic girdles.
Classify joints as fibrous, cartilaginous and synovial with examples.
Match types of synovial joints with their locations in the body.

topics.title: Disorders of muscular and skeletal system

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the causes and features of myasthenia gravis, muscular dystrophy and tetany.
Identify the causes and features of arthritis, osteoporosis and gout.

topics.title: Neural system and the human neural system

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the organisation of the neural system differs among Hydra, insects and vertebrates.
Distinguish the central and peripheral neural systems and afferent and efferent nerve fibres.
Distinguish the somatic and autonomic divisions of the peripheral neural system by the organs they serve.
Identify the cell body, dendrites, axon and synaptic knobs of a neuron and their roles.
Classify neurons as multipolar, bipolar or unipolar and state where each is found.
Distinguish myelinated and non-myelinated nerve fibres and state where each occurs.

topics.title: Generation and conduction of nerve impulse

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how ion permeability and the sodium-potassium pump polarise the resting axonal membrane.
Explain depolarisation by Na+ influx and repolarisation by K+ efflux during an action potential.
Explain how local current flow conducts an action potential along an axon.
Describe the structure and speed of impulse transmission at electrical synapses.
Explain the sequence of events in impulse transmission across a chemical synapse.

topics.title: Central neural system: brain protection and forebrain

concepts.learning_objective: State the functions of the brain and name the cranial meninges in order.
Describe the cerebral hemispheres, corpus callosum, cerebral cortex and white matter.
State the functions of the thalamus, hypothalamus and limbic system.
Describe the location of the midbrain, the cerebral aqueduct and the corpora quadrigemina.
State the structure and functions of the pons, cerebellum and medulla oblongata.
Identify the parts of the brain stem and predict the effects of damage to it.

topics.title: Endocrine glands, hormones and the hypothalamus

concepts.learning_objective: Define endocrine glands and hormones using the current scientific definition of a hormone.
Explain how hypothalamic releasing and inhibiting hormones control the pituitary gland.
Identify the hormones of the pars distalis, pars intermedia and pars nervosa and their actions.
Relate gigantism, dwarfism, acromegaly and diabetes insipidus to faulty pituitary hormone secretion.
State the role of pineal melatonin in regulating 24-hour body rhythms.
Describe the functions of thyroid hormones and the disorders caused by their under- or over-secretion.
Explain how PTH and thyrocalcitonin together regulate blood calcium levels.
State the role of thymosins in cell-mediated and humoral immunity.
Describe the emergency actions of adrenaline and noradrenaline.
Distinguish glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids by their main examples and actions.
Explain how insulin and glucagon jointly maintain blood glucose and what goes wrong in diabetes mellitus.
Describe the source and functions of androgens secreted by the testis.
Describe the sources and functions of estrogen and progesterone.

topics.title: Hormones of heart, kidney and gastrointestinal tract

concepts.learning_objective: State the source and action of atrial natriuretic factor and erythropoietin.
Match gastrin, secretin, CCK and GIP with their targets and actions.
Explain the specificity of hormone receptors and the difference between membrane-bound and intracellular receptors.
Classify hormones by chemical nature and relate each class to its mode of action.
